source.title: Does SGD really happen in tiny subspaces?
source.authors: Minhak Song; Kwangjun Ahn; Chulhee Yun

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests whether projected gradient updates in the Hessian dominant subspace train networks, and finds they fail to decrease training loss while bulk projections remain effective. This refines the broader training claim for a particular subspace-based intervention.
record.gate_note: Reports results for dominant/bulk projected updates, alignment measurements, and optimizer comparisons. Cited results from earlier work are not extracted as rows. Figure-only loss and alignment values are recorded without reading numeric values from plots.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces V5's full-batch edge-of-stability result using training loss and Hessian eigenvalues: sharpness rises to and stabilizes near 2/η while ordinary GD continues reducing loss (Figure 9; Appendix E, Figures 29–31). Its principal subspace-projection findings concern a different claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: dominant-projected updates fail to further reduce training loss across the tested optimizers, while tested bulk projections remain effective. The authors attribute alignment in gradient-flow SGD primarily to stochastic noise interacting with an ill-conditioned landscape, and alignment in edge-of-stability GD to self-stabilization.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Hessian-eigenspace projections and alignment during optimization, rather than initialization, width, depth, normalization, or learning-rate recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment and projected-update outcomes vary with optimizer and regime: SGD versus full-batch GD in the gradient-flow regime; dominant versus bulk projections; EoS and SAM regimes; momentum and adaptive methods. In the noise experiments, higher noise and smaller batch sizes increase alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Dominant-projected optimizer updates fail to sustain loss reduction, while tested bulk-projected updates retain loss reduction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested settings, dominant Hessian-subspace alignment does not imply that projecting updates into that subspace preserves training progress.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient alignment depends on stochastic noise and optimization regime; switching between SGD and GD changes alignment, and greater noise increases it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dominant Hessian-subspace alignment can arise through stochastic noise in the gradient-flow regime or self-stabilization at the edge of stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Momentum and adaptive methods amplify bulk effective learning rates, which positively correlate with training speed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bulk effective learning rate is associated with optimization speed across the tested GD and Adam variants.

record.code_released: Source code is included in attached supplementary material; URL not stated.
record.problems: Most central loss and alignment outcomes are qualitative statements or plots without reported numeric values or uncertainty estimates. Main datasets are subsets (MNIST-5k, CIFAR10-5k, SST2-1k); no CIFAR-100, corrupted-label, or random-label results. The paper calls generalization tests preliminary and leaves systematic study for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Figure-only outcomes without descriptive values are included only where the accompanying text supports a trend; no numeric values were read from plots.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, special initialization for deep plain networks, and Fixup.
Comparisons of initialization, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit, the catapult loss-rise/curvature-drop sequence, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Ordinary full-batch GD jointly exhibits sharpness rising to and stabilizing near 2/η and continued training-loss reduction. Add separate rows for MLP/MNIST-5k, CNN/CIFAR10-5k, and Transformer/SST2-1k; the respective thresholds are 20, 200, and 400. Existing rows record projected updates or alignment instead.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Figure 9a/c; Appendix B.3; Appendix E, Figures 29 and 31.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Its ordinary-GD edge-of-stability results support that version despite the reader's not-tested designation. Failures after deliberately projecting updates do not challenge the stated standard-optimizer claims. States marked cannot_determine for unrelated rows concern applicability to V1–V6, not whether the reported subspace effects occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularization recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and width comparisons.
Depth effects, residual shortcuts, and shortcut-free deep network training.
Learning rates above the stability limit and sharpness behavior as stated in the version.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance; Fixup.
